title: Send personal note to Mauro De Gennaro: account language preference left to JMAP account settings (drafted, not sent)
description:
Personal note to Mauro De Gennaro (Stalwart; mail-sharing and metadata drafts; owns the IETF 126 action on JMAP account settings, on the IETF 127 AOB agenda with Hans-Joerg). Revised 2026-11-15: preferredLanguages was dropped from draft-atwood-jmap-updates-00, so this note now hands the account language preference to the settings work instead of asking whether to merge. Mauro raised "locale preferences" on the list on 2026-02-10 (https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/jmap/bMiAFWFW2-N6aikkw-mvZ4UbndI/, verified). NOT SENT; needs Mark's explicit approval. Ideally send BEFORE Thursday's session, after the list email (jmap-chat-spec-0577). Replace LIST-THREAD-URL. Consider cc'ing Hans-Joerg once his address is confirmed (not in the local spec library).

--------

From: Mark Atwood <mark@reviewcommit.com>
To: Mauro De Gennaro <mauro@stalw.art>
Subject: Account language preference: leaving it to JMAP account settings

Hi Mauro,

I saw that JMAP account settings is on Thursday's agenda, and that you
mentioned locale preferences on the list back in February. My new
draft, draft-atwood-jmap-updates-00 (LIST-THREAD-URL), adds localized
display text to JMAP. An earlier version also defined an account-level
language preference, but that's clearly an account setting, so I took
it out and left it to your work.

One use case you might want to cover: text the server writes with no
request in progress, such as push notification text or a message sent
on the user's behalf. There's no Accept-Language to go by then, so the
server needs the user's preferred languages from somewhere. A list of
language tags, most preferred first, would be enough for that.

The same draft also makes Principal name and description localizable
(RFC 9670), which touches the sharing work. As a Stalwart implementer,
your view on whether the localization model is easy to implement
would be very useful.

Thanks,
Mark
